summary: Production planning domain foundation adds approved work definitions, MRP planned-order proposal metadata, production-release preparation metadata, and SAP PP parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable persistence, live MRP runtime, finite scheduling, shop-floor execution, inventory mutation, procurement purchase orders, accounting posting, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.

findings: The implementation is a small pure-domain validation/calculation model, not a live MRP/scheduler/MES or ERP monolith clone.
Work definition, MRP netting, lot sizing, material availability, and capacity checks are deterministic guard-clause logic with no hidden side effects.
Flat production-planning microservice destination improves SAP PP parity without creating microservices/erp.
Capability flags and evidence rows keep runtime/shop-floor/inventory/cloud claims honest until adapters land.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if missing work-definition approval, missing planned-order proposal, material shortage, capacity shortage, invalid dates, unsafe refs, credential-shaped evidence refs, invalid horizons, or zero quantities are accepted.
findings: Positive plan-to-produce flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to work definitions, BOM/route/work-center approval, MRP planned orders, and production-release preparation concepts common to production-planning systems.
Focused production-planning tests/clippy, ERP parity map tests/clippy, 29-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan are recorded in verification.

alternatives_named: leave production planning as a parity gap
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives ERP PP parity a service-owned first write path while keeping MRP runtime, schedulers, shop-floor execution, storage, inventory movement, Workflow, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Leaving PP as a gap weakens ERP parity after procurement and warehouse foundations landed.
Live MRP/MES/runtime requires durable state, job orchestration, shop-floor integrations, and operational SLOs beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, shop-floor channels, procurement calls, or inventory/accounting mutations are introduced.
Source and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/date/quantity validation and arithmetic only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, scheduler runtime, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL component counts, run minutes, demand, stock, planned order, material, and capacity quantities
findings: SAP/Oracle/Microsoft official materials inform production-planning coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-production-planning-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable production-planning spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
New code is isolated to microservices/production-planning plus Enterprise Suite parity map references.
Clean architecture is preserved: domain crate depends only on data boundary kernel and std.
No new third-party dependencies were added; Cargo.lock changed only for the new workspace package.
specs/microservices/production-planning.json parses successfully and evidence follows prior multispectrum shape.
MRP net requirement, lot-size rounding, material availability, and capacity checks are deterministic arithmetic with no hidden state.

M1_challenge_assumption.finding: Challenged whether production planning should wait for live inventory storage; creating a separate PP domain is more aligned with ERP parity and keeps inventory mutation in warehouse boundaries.

M2_zoomed_out_fit.finding: Complements HR/payroll/accounting/procurement/treasury/warehouse foundations and improves ERP parity while keeping no microservices/erp monolith.
